To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACT-R architecture is well suited to model human performance in complex dynamic task, that it provides a straightforward account of human multi-tasking behavior, that it provides an account of cognitive workload based upon the architecture's primitives and that it can be ported to HLA without undue effort.
the ACT-R architecture can be used as a platform for developing human performance models, and that the resulting model can be easily and efficiently ported to HLA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a human performance model based on a cognitive architecture that is portable to HLA and can provide a foundation for the development of a cognitive workload model.
the design of a cognitive model of a simplified air-traffic-control task.
the development of an architecture-based model of human performance that is both simple and accurate, and can be readily ported to HLA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a cognitive architecture for the development of human performance models greatly simplifies the model design and implementation process.
a human performance model implemented in ACT-R is a very efficient way of modeling human performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cognitive architecture can provide a highly efficient and flexible framework for human performance modeling.
the use of a well-developed and well-understood cognitive architecture provided a highly accurate and efficient human performance model.
the use of a well-developed, cognitive architecture greatly simplified model development, while providing accurate predictions of human performance, and a straightforward implementation of HLA. 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a well-developed, cognitive architecture greatly simplifies the development of complex human performance models.
a well-developed and well-documented cognitive architecture, such as ACT-R, provides a powerful and flexible framework for the development of human performance models. 1
cognitive architectures are an ideal basis for the development of human performance models, and can provide a solid foundation for the development of HLA-enabled human models.
